market_view: The S&P 500 rose 0.28% to a record 7,743.98 after the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% (10-2, two dissents for a hike) with the 10-year back above 5%; after hours the megacap split widened, with Microsoft up ~3% on a 48% Azure beat and lower-than-expected capex, while Alphabet fell ~10% to ~$288 on an EPS miss (SpaceX mark-down, negative FCF) and ServiceNow (-15-18%) and Fortinet (-24-26%) were punished despite raised outlooks. Thursday brings Q3 GDP and Lilly before the open and Amazon after the close, so I'm not adding correlated megacap risk; the operator's standing orders (updates/ALL.md) only shape research and writing and were followed.
lessons: GOOGL is my worst position and the playbook's top loser list is full of it (Grok -10.28%, ChatGPT -9.47% both stopped), and now it is gapping ~10% below my $308 stop after hours. I bought a 'cheap at 17x' megacap ahead of a capex-heavy print with no stop logic for earnings gaps; for compounders I will now either enter after the report or size the stop for the earnings gap, and I still won't widen a stop on a loser.

I'm still not beating the Fruit Fly: my alpha is -0.88% per trade over 79 trades (95% range -1.78% to +0.02%, 2.2% chance of beating random) versus the Fly's +0.23%, and my moonshot book stays the reliable weak spot (n=40, 15% win rate, -1.21%). So again zero moonshots; no edge claimed.

Buying good news after a one-session selloff is two for two for me (GM +4.79%, UNH +5.35%; a hunch, n<20), but tonight's candidates don't fit cleanly: Garmin's -6.8% came with in-line revenue, a tariff-refund-flattered margin and a 27x multiple with a ~$288 Hold-consensus target, and ServiceNow/Fortinet are after-hours gaps, which the lab says lose another -2.1% open-to-close (n=25). So I pass rather than force a catalyst trade.

review.reason: Q3 EPS missed badly ($2.12-2.67 vs ~$3.02) on an ~$8B SpaceX mark-down plus heavier depreciation, FCF turned negative, and management guided 2027 capex significantly higher; shares fell ~10% after hours from $322.22 to ~$288, below my $308 stop, so the cost-of-AI thesis is impaired and I exit at the open rather than widen the stop.

Double beat (revenue $92.28B vs ~$90.6B, Azure +48%), capex ~$39.4B below the ~$45.9B expected, and a Q2 revenue guide of $96.0-97.1B above consensus sent shares up ~3% after hours; I raise the stop to $505 to protect the position while leaving room for a volatile post-earnings tech session.

Reports Thursday after the close; Alphabet's capex-driven selloff is a risk to the AI-spend read-through but Microsoft's beat shows the market still rewards cloud growth with capex discipline, and the $238 stop stays ~6% below.
Flat to entry with no company-specific news since the Q3 inflow beat and TD Cowen upgrade; a record S&P close supports AUM-linked fees, and the $1,030 stop remains ~9% away.

Q3 is due Thursday before the open against consensus EPS around $7.11 and a ~$8.71 whisper (Finviz, Oct 21); the GLP-1 thesis is intact and the $1,190 stop sits ~7% below, outside a normal earnings-day range, so I hold through the print.
